title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. Design: N = 240 paired tasks drawn from a public synthetic NetOps task bank (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks), requested generator gpt-5-mini, deterministic pybatfish-style validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair call per task). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms), producing model_calls_used = 240 (shared generation) and planned_episode_count = 480 (completed_episode_count = 480). Results: every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240; n10 = n01 = n00 = 0). The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration→execution deviations materially limit inference and are reported explicitly: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation, and (2) a prespecified primary comparison (GVR vs schema-constrained decoding, C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit in this artifact-backed setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. We release the archived artifacts and recommend deterministic reruns under independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model evaluation, and expanded verifier coverage to evaluate GVR’s operational value under conditions that restore discordance potential.

sections.introduction:
LLM-driven automation for network operations (NetOps) aims to translate operator intent to device configurations. However, stochastic generation can produce outputs that are syntactically plausible but semantically incorrect relative to network invariants (reachability, workflow preconditions, ACL/policy constraints). Prior work therefore advocates architectures that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair loops—commonly described as generate–verify–repair (GVR)—to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects before committing changes.

We carried out a preregistered paired experiment to test a narrow, operational question: does a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (GVR) reduce validator-detected semantic violations for intent→configuration tasks relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding? The study was preregistered (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1; preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d) and executed under a frozen adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) and analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and authoritative for reported numbers.

We report the execution accounting, confirmatory outcomes, explicit preregistration→execution deviations, statistical interpretation of a degenerate contingency, and concrete reproducible recommendations grounded in the archived evidence.
sections.related_work:
Three strands frame our study. First, cross-domain surveys and empirical studies document LLM hallucinations and incorrect structured outputs for code and configuration tasks, motivating verifier-interposed pipelines (see evidence_synthesis claims C1–C3). Second, generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding architectures have been shown to improve mechanically checkable properties (compilation, grammar validity) in prior benchmarks and case studies, though semantic guarantees at the domain level remain open (evidence_synthesis C2–C3). Third, NetOps work emphasizes verifier-driven evaluation, intent-based translation, and human-in-the-loop governance as mitigations for operational risk. Our run differs in being preregistered, paired, and artifact-archived; it evaluates whether a bounded GVR intervention adds verifier-detectable value under the exact execution semantics and task distribution recorded in the archive.

Nearest prior systems include intent-driven NetOps prototypes (NetConfEval-style work), GVR-like generator+validator systems in code generation, and NetOps-specific verifier-integration reports. Those studies report benefits under their chosen semantics and oracles; importantly, measurable gains depend on the generator’s baseline error rate and the oracle’s coverage. We position this experiment as a controlled, preregistered accounting: it tests a narrowly prespecified estimand under a precisely recorded execution contract rather than providing a broad multi-model benchmark.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: The preregistration defined the primary estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation rate, computed in paired fashion). Two prespecified primary comparisons were registered: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding, with Bonferroni correction across the two comparisons (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 was frozen prior to execution.

Task bank and oracle: The public synthetic NetOps task bank (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks = 240 tasks) encodes initial device states, intents, workflow constraints, and reference final states. The deterministic validator used a pybatfish-style oracle (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that returns structured diagnostics including violation_count and parsed_command_count. The scoring rule was full_intent_constraint_validation as implemented in validator_version 5.0.

Execution contract and critical semantics: The frozen execution contract requested generator = gpt-5-mini and constrained repair budget (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Crucially, the executed generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1), meaning a single initial generation per task was reused across both arms (baseline and guarded). Model- and execution-level accounting from the manifest: planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; complete_pair_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240 (shared generation). All of these items are archived and authoritative.

Analysis and prespecified sensitivity: Primary test was a paired McNemar-style exact test with paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation (so that within-pair discordance could arise); this assumption is explicitly violated by the executed shared-generation semantics and thereby invalidates the preregistered power justification for the observed run.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): Execution completed as planned: planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; model_calls_used = 240 (one shared generation per task). Missingness and contamination summaries report zero failures and zero flags.

Primary confirmatory outcomes: For every task the shared initial candidate satisfied the deterministic validator in both arms. The paired contingency observed by the analysis executor was n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Summary rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; 10,000 resamples; seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, analysis_log.jsonl) are archived and authoritative for these numbers.

Repair-loop diagnostics: For every episode validator_trace.repair_applied = false; the bounded repair loop never executed because there were no validator-detected failures to trigger a repair. Representative per-task scoring JSONs confirm identical shared-initial candidates and identical validation_before/validation_after blocks with violation_count = 0.

Statistical interpretation of degeneracy: The observed contingency is degenerate—zero discordant pairs—so the paired test has no within-pair information to estimate differential effect. The reported p-value and CI are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency under the preregistered analysis executor. Practically, when both arms always pass the same validator check the paired estimand is exactly zero and the test cannot detect improvements that require discordant outcomes to exist. This degeneracy tracks directly to the shared_initial_candidate semantics and to the generator+prompt pairing’s empirical success on the synthetic task bank.
sections.discussion:
Conservative operational interpretation: Under the exact execution semantics—single shared generation per task, single-model generator (gpt-5-mini), single bounded repair attempt, and the deterministic validator used—bounded GVR provided no additional validator-detectable value because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. Two artifact-supported mechanisms explain the null outcome. First, task/verifier alignment: the synthetic task bank, generator+prompting pairing, and the validator together defined a distribution the generator deterministically satisfied across all sampled tasks. Second, evaluation semantics: shared-initial-candidate generation removes stochastic variation between arms and thus eliminates the within-pair discordance that a GVR intervention could exploit.

Preregistration→execution deviations and their effects (explicit): (A) Generation semantics mismatch: the preregistration’s power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; executed shared-generation semantics (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false) removed the primary source of within-pair discordance, invalidating that power justification for the observed run. (B) Unexecuted prespecified comparison: the preregistration listed two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B); the archived execution recorded only the adapter-configured experiment comparing unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) and did not execute the prespecified schema-constrained baseline comparison (C vs B). No recorded rationale for the omission appears in the archive. Both deviations are disclosed and affect the scope of inferential claims.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is limited by the generation-semantics mismatch and by the single-model, single-prompt pairing. Construct validity is limited by the validator’s coverage: passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not guarantee absence of operational risks outside the encoded invariants. External validity is limited by synthetic tasks, single generator (gpt-5-mini), single repair budget (one attempt), and the single verifier implementation. Conclusion validity is constrained by zero discordant outcomes, which preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics.

Reproducible next steps supported by archived artifacts: (1) Re-run the preregistered paired design with independent per-condition generation (set independent_condition_generation = true and allow separate generator calls per arm) using the same task manifest and RNG seeds archived in the run to restore discordance potential. (2) Inject adversarial or golden-reference tasks (10% planned in preregistration) so the oracle’s sensitivity can be validated and not overwhelmed by generator success on benign tasks. (3) Expand the model scope beyond gpt-5-mini and increase repair budgets to measure repair dynamics. (4) Broaden verifier coverage (additional semantic predicates or formal hybrids) to reduce oracle incompleteness risk. The archive includes the task manifest, RNG seeds, model configuration (requested_model = gpt-5-mini; model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), and analysis executor configuration to support deterministic reruns.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics, every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a null paired estimate and a degenerate statistical outcome. Two preregistration→execution deviations (shared-generation vs preregistered independent generation; an unexecuted prespecified comparison) materially limit inference. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR did not add verifier-detectable value in this specific, artifact-backed setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. We publish the authoritative archived artifacts to enable deterministic reruns under independent-generation, adversarial, and multi-model regimes that are necessary to evaluate GVR’s operational value more broadly.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
